payload.rebuttal: fixed: Confirmed the bug. When a citation's own clause was empty, line 148 set `prev_clause_names = clause_names`, storing the literal empty clause rather than the fallback names just used. A third citation in the same sentence with no intervening backticked identifier then found both its own clause and the stored fallback empty, so it got no names and `_construct_defect` passed it unconditionally, skipping the construct check. Changed line 148 to `prev_clause_names = names`, carrying the resolved value forward so the fallback survives any number of consecutive empty clauses, matching criterion 2's rule. Added a three-citation regression case to `test_citation_defects_scope_names_to_each_citations_own_clause` (`_diff` sits in three places over `mod/lib.py:4`, `:5`, `:21`), verified it fails on the prior code and passes on the fix, and confirmed `ruff`, `ty`, the tree-wide `prose` check and the full test suite (4614 passed) are clean on the new commit.
